summary: All 44 functional requirements, 13 success criteria, acceptance scenarios and contracts are implemented in the diff (render drift green, six roles reference engineering.md, .specify/ untouched, DESIGN.md leads, run's own commits correctly exempt from Red: lines), except four gaps: a dangling commit-body reference in the shipped spec-conformance role, FR-018's conventional-default constraint dropped from the planning role, ENG-6's yields nuance missing from the reference, and the plan's reason table omitting the SpecKit scaffolding files.

findings.summary: The shipped spec-conformance role (and its four dist copies) points at `<F>/references/commit-body.md`, a file that does not exist in `core/skills/factory/references/` or any harness tree; the commit-body contract lives only in this run's `specs/001-tdd-engineering-rules/contracts/commit-body.md`, so every future run resolves the link to a missing file.
findings.evidence: core/roles/spec-conformance.md line 20: "rests on the two accepted `Red:` forms in [commit-body](<F>/references/commit-body.md)" — but `ls core/skills/factory/references/` shows only engineering.md, findings.md, protocol.md, state.md, verbs.md (same in dist/<harness>/skill/references/). tasks.md T009 cites `contracts/commit-body.md`, the run-local artifact, not a shipped reference; the role text substituted a path that does not exist. Impact is contained because the same sentence restates the unparseable rule and engineering.md's "Red proof" section carries both forms, so the check stays performable — hence medium, not high.
findings.fix: Point the link at the shipped authority instead: "rests on the two accepted `Red:` forms in `<F>/references/engineering.md` (Red proof)" in core/roles/spec-conformance.md, then re-render all four harnesses and commit dist/ with the source change.

findings.summary: FR-018's requirement that the plan pick the language's conventional default test runner is missing from the planning role's stage instruction, so a future plan could name any runner and still conform to the shipped text.
findings.evidence: FR-018: "MUST pick the language's conventional default runner, naming the choice and the reason"; tasks.md T006(a) mandates `Test runner: <runner> - <why>` "only when the repository has none (the language's conventional default, so the user can object at the approver gate)"; contracts/plan-artifact.md line 21: "the plan names the language's conventional default and the reason". But core/roles/spec-builder.md line 31 says only "`Test runner: <runner> - <why>` only when the repository has none (so the user can object at the approver gate)" — the conventional-default constraint was dropped in implementation. The runner-setup-first-task half of FR-018 is present (tasks override: "when the repository has no test runner, the runner-setup task is task 1").
findings.fix: Restore the constraint in the plan-stage override of core/roles/spec-builder.md: "`Test runner: <runner> - <why>` only when the repository has none — the language's conventional default, named with the reason so the user can object at the approver gate"; re-render and commit dist/.

findings.summary: ENG-6 in the shipped reference omits the nuance the contract table and the spec's edge case require: extending a close-but-not-exact-fit function is preferred over a near-duplicate, and a genuinely different concern may be new code with the difference stated.
findings.evidence: spec.md Edge Cases: "An existing function that is close but not an exact fit: extending it is preferred over a near-duplicate; a genuinely different concern may be new code, with the difference stated"; contracts/engineering-reference.md ENG-6 row, yields column: "Nothing; a genuinely different concern may be new code, with the difference stated"; tasks.md T003 requires the rules "verbatim in the meaning of the rule-set table". engineering.md line 12 says only "reuse or extend an existing one that fits" — the near-duplicate preference and the stated difference are absent (ENG-7..ENG-9 do carry their yields sentences, so ENG-6's omission is inconsistent).
findings.fix: Append one sentence to ENG-6 in engineering.md: "A close but not exact fit is extended rather than duplicated; a genuinely different concern may be new code, with the difference stated." Re-render and commit dist/.

findings.summary: The plan's "Reasons for new files, abstractions and dependencies" section, which claims to carry a reason for every new file this change introduces (FR-020b worked example), omits the SpecKit scaffolding the branch adds: the `.specify/` tree and `.claude/skills/speckit-*` skills.
findings.evidence: git diff origin/main...HEAD adds 22 files under .specify/ and 15 under .claude/skills/speckit-* (first added in commit af818f4 "factory: start"), yet plan.md's reason table (lines 64–71) lists only engineering.md, the dist copies, CONTEXT.md/ADRs and the specs artifacts — no row covers the SpecKit scaffolding, so the plan's own FR-020b completeness claim ("finds a stated reason for every one of them") does not hold for these files.
findings.fix: Add one row to the plan's reason table for `.specify/` and `.claude/skills/speckit-*`: run-bootstrap scaffolding the speckit stages the planning role invokes require in this repository; documentation/configuration only, produced once at branch start.
